clue.text: Massage ace, out now for hot dog

indicators.note: the ace goes out and something else now stands in its place, so the clue signals a swap of one letter for another

parts.note: shiatzu is a less common spelling of shiatsu, the Japanese finger-pressure massage
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A spa advert: the star masseur has left, so get a hot dog instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The massage must be spelt SHIATZU, an accepted variant, for the swap to work. 'Hot dog' looks like one food item; 'hot' is the H and 'dog' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small long-haired toy breed of Tibetan and Chinese origin, so it is one kind of dog.

clue.text: Very pissed, breaking the clock

indicators.note: one word breaking into another splits it open, so the second word sits inside the first

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'
pissed in its literal sense means urinated, which is peed

explanation.surface: A drunk is so far gone that they smash the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' reads as British slang for drunk, but the wordplay wants its literal sense, urinated.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedometer, shortened, is the dial on a car's dashboard that British drivers informally call the clock.

clue.text: Compiler's commuting maybe? Not on foot

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who says I am of himself; the apostrophe s stands for am

indicators.note: not on means the little word on is to be left out of what comes before

parts.note: commuting might mean being on a bus

explanation.surface: The setter explains that his commute is by bus, not on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' asks for the little word to be dropped from the commuting phrase. 'Foot' looks like the walking alternative to the bus, but it is the definition: a unit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a metrical foot is a group of syllables; this one is a short syllable followed by a long one.

clue.text: Cistern with lid off was minging

indicators.note: taking the lid off a down answer removes its top letter

parts.note: minging is British slang for foul-smelling, so was minging means smelt bad

explanation.surface: A complaint that the water cistern stank once someone lifted its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the lid is the first letter, so 'lid off' drops the S. MINGING is British slang for smelly or disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a large container for storing water or other liquid, and the answer names such a vessel.

clue.text: Employed top man at Washington Post?

parts.note: Washington is the capital and seat of the government of the United States, abbreviated US
the top man at a newspaper is its editor, ED for short

explanation.surface: A question about the chief editor of The Washington Post newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of an American paper would be a US editor, and 'Post' only completes the newspaper's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Employed as a past tense or participle means put to work or made use of, a straight synonym.

clue.text: During course of stress, middle son's no good, then rallies

indicators.note: during the course of a word means somewhere within it, so then goes inside
middle picks out the S in the middle of stress as the one to be replaced

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son; with the apostrophe s it reads as the son is no good

explanation.surface: A family drama: the middle son is a disappointment, then he bounces back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle son's no good' is read as 'the middle son becomes no good', a replacement; 'During course of' then signals an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover or reinforce, so rallies, as a verb, means makes or grows stronger.

clue.text: Tip for old schoolmarm out of make-up?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, describing something of one's genetic make-up

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged
the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice to an old schoolmistress that she should go without cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests cosmetics; here it is the genetic make-up held in chromosomes. The tip of 'old' gives O, which is mixed up with SCHOOLMARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic make-up is carried in the threads of DNA within a cell nucleus, so this adjective describes that constitution.

clue.text: At intervals, turn wheel … lap of Mull futile

indicators.note: taking letters at intervals means picking every second one, skipping the rest

explanation.surface: A cyclist circling the Isle of Mull finds turning the wheel lap after lap pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull is an island in the Scottish Hebrides. Every second letter of 'turn wheel lap of Mull' spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile effort achieves nothing, and the answer describes something that gives no help or assistance.

clue.text: Putting the lid on the whisky?

definitions.text: Putting the lid on the whisky?

parts.words: Putting the lid on the whisky?
parts.note: putting the lid on means stopping or quashing something; read playfully, it is adding Scotch whisky with an -ing ending

explanation.surface: Someone corks the whisky bottle at the end of the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the lid on a rumour or plan is to quash it decisively, which is exactly this verb's sense.

clue.text: What fire drill's doing at Westminster finance office?

parts.note: a fire drill empties a building, which is clearing it
the House of Commons sits at Westminster in London

explanation.surface: A question about the purpose of a fire drill at Parliament's finance office.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament, whose chambers are each called the House.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks settle cheques and accounts with one another through a central institution of this kind, a financial office.

clue.text: "The Messiah" Keano & co in the heart of the melee

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another
the heart of a phrase is what is left once its outer letters are cut away

parts.note: Keano is Roy Keane, former captain of Manchester United, Man U for short

explanation.surface: A football fan hails Roy Keane as a messiah amid a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Keane, nicknamed Keano, led Manchester United (Man U) and was known for his fierce tackling, hence 'melee'. The central four letters of 'the melee' wrap around MANU.
explanation.definitionFit: The name, meaning 'God with us', is a biblical title prophesied for the Messiah in Isaiah and applied to Christ.

clue.text: Soup du jour? Its trimmings sustain First Lady on run

indicators.note: to sustain is to hold up from either side, so the outer letters enclose the rest
the trimmings of the phrase du jour are its outermost letters

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Book of Genesis
to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A menu note about the soup of the day being served to the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soup du jour' looks like one menu phrase, but 'Soup' alone is the definition and 'du jour' gives its trimmings D and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is old photographers' slang for the chemical bath in which a film or print is processed.

clue.text: Diamonds, something difficult to beat

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit
a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A card player calls the diamond suit something hard to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' seems part of the phrase 'difficult to beat'; it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent thoroughly is to thrash or trounce them, the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Wife separating POTUS and PM on TV makes way clearer

indicators.note: a letter separating two words stands between them, inside the pair

parts.note: POTUS, President of the United States, could be George Bush
Jim Hacker is the Prime Minister in the BBC sitcom Yes, Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A spouse comes between a President and a Prime Minister to ease negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: Jim Hacker was the hapless politician of the British TV comedies Yes Minister and Yes, Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hacks a path through dense scrub or forest, so clears a route through the bush.

clue.text: Spook agent receiving shocking treatment having landed by river

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the agent holds the rest inside

parts.note: an agent can be a spy
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock
alit is a past form of alight, to land

explanation.surface: A secret agent, back on land by a river, is given electric shock treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spook' suggests another word for spy, matching 'agent'; here it means a ghost or ghostliness.
explanation.definitionFit: A spook is a ghost, and the abstract noun names a phantom or the quality of being ghostly.

clue.text: Travelling fans say who might be contacted after breaking down? AA?

definitions.meaning: away supporters travelling together form organised clubs of fans

definitions.text: who might be contacted after breaking down? AA?
definitions.meaning: AA is both the Automobile Association, rung after a car breaks down, and Alcoholics Anonymous, for someone who has broken down

explanation.surface: Football fans on the road wonder whom to call when the coach breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: AA serves twice: the Automobile Association is Britain's main roadside breakdown service; Alcoholics Anonymous helps after an emotional breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are bodies offering help to members: fans' associations backing a club and self-help networks for people in difficulty.

clue.text: Lie to schoolgirl doing audition?

indicators.note: audition is the act of hearing, so this signals a word as it is heard

parts.note: a schoolgirl is a miss in form, a girl in a school class

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl fibs while trying out for the school play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing audition' reads as trying out for a part; 'audition' here means hearing. In Britain a 'form' is a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie to someone is to give them false information deliberately, the same sense as the verb.

clue.text: Unable to work with personnel east of mine? He's an old man

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means to the right of, coming after

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
the word he is taken as it stands, with the apostrophe s as a link

indicators.note: with means holding, so one pair of pieces holds the other between them

parts.note: unable means cannot, contracted to can't
an opus is a work, especially of music
HR, Human Resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A worker can't cope with the human resources people at the coal mine and asks who the old man is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' sounds like a boss or father; here it is an early fossil human.
explanation.definitionFit: Java Man, an extinct early hominid now classed as Homo erectus, was once given this genus name, an ancient human.

clue.text: Tweedsmuir creation: take one for nothing, I have it in white

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for take, as on a prescription (recipe)
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping it in its place

parts.note: Chardonnay is a white wine
O is the figure nought, nothing
ha is an exclamation of discovery, a cry of I have it

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction for Tweedsmuir's creation: substitute and mix it into white.
explanation.walkthrough: John Buchan, the Scottish author of thrillers, became Lord Tweedsmuir. 'Take' is the prescription abbreviation R, from Latin recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of The Thirty-Nine Steps and later thrillers was created by John Buchan, the novelist later ennobled as Baron Tweedsmuir.

clue.text: I'm very surprised indeed about northbound track

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: yes means indeed, as an emphatic agreement

indicators.note: in a down answer going north means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: to dog someone is to track or follow them

explanation.surface: A railway passenger is astonished by a track heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' suggests railway lines; here it is the verb dog, which 'northbound' turns to GOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic exclamation is a cry of astonishment, the equivalent of saying how amazed one is.

clue.text: Boris's repetition accepted for now

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Boris Johnson was the Prime Minister when this was set; PM with the apostrophe s for is or has
rote is learning by repetition

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's habit of repeating himself is tolerated for the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was Britain's Prime Minister in 2020, when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation means temporarily, for the time being.

clue.text: Tragic figure, Romeo, getting over end of Juliet in sad tale

indicators.note: sad in the sense of sorry or wretched signals the letters are rearranged
Romeo getting over the end letter means it is put in its place, covering it
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo gets over Juliet's death in a sad tale of tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The T in TALE, which is also Juliet's last letter, gives way to R, making RALE; 'sad' shuffles that. Romeo suggests Shakespeare's lovers, but the figure is from another tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's aged king, broken by his daughters, is the title character of one of his great tragedies.

clue.text: Not in the pink, clearly

definitions.meaning: in the pink means in good health, so not in it means unwell
taken literally, something with its colour off is clear, transparent

explanation.surface: A judgement that someone obviously isn't feeling well.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly unwell is described as looking out of sorts and pale, the opposite of being healthy and rosy.

clue.text: Welsh resort's babbling brook?

definitions.note: the definition with the apostrophe s for is

indicators.note: babbling is speech, so the word is as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: a rill is a small brook or stream

explanation.surface: A Welsh seaside town is known for its babbling brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Babbling brook' is a stock phrase; 'babbling' is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town on the North Wales coast in Denbighshire, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Characters predominantly seen working in milk float

indicators.note: predominantly is read as pre-dominant, the leading characters of each word

explanation.surface: Letters painted on the side of a milk float, the electric delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is a British electric milk-delivery van; 'float' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To float is to stay up on water, and the answer's verb also means to be buoyed up in liquid.

clue.text: Vessel that stole into street

indicators.note: into puts the pieces inside the street

parts.note: how can mean that, as in dialect 'he said as how'
a boa is a long scarf or stole of feathers or fur

explanation.surface: A boat that a thief stole from the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like the verb steal; it is the fur wrap, a boa.
explanation.definitionFit: A river steamer carrying a theatre troupe, so a vessel of the kind found on the Mississippi.

clue.text: Scientist's clerical error originally included

definitions.note: the definition with the apostrophe s for is

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so the letter goes within the word

parts.note: clerical means relating to clergy, so priestly

indicators.note: originally means at its origin, the first letter

explanation.surface: A clerical error from a scientist slipped into the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clerical error' is a stock phrase for a slip of the pen; here clerical means of the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Priestley, the English chemist and clergyman, is credited with discovering oxygen.

clue.text: Spooner's giving you a little fruit wedge?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: some means a little, as in 'have some'
a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a slice of fruit by the eccentric Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of the answer's two words and it sounds like 'sump lum', that is 'some plum'. A wedge is slang for a large wad of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge or wodge of money is a large single payment, paid all at once.
